WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"And when he heard say of Tirhakah king of Ethiopia, Behold, he is come out to fight against thee: he sent messengers again unto Hezekiah." 2 Kings 19:9
Isaiah's book gives the same report in nearly the same words. Isaiah 37:9

Before this, Rab-shakeh had mocked Judah's trust in Egypt: "thou trustest upon the staff of this bruised reed, even upon Egypt ... so is Pharaoh king of Egypt unto all that trust on him". He names no Pharaoh. 2 Kings 18:21 Isaiah 36:6
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
Hezekiah spread Sennacherib's letter before the LORD and prayed. 2 Kings 19:14–19
Rab-shakeh accused Hezekiah of putting his "trust on Egypt for chariots and for horsemen". 2 Kings 18:24 Isaiah 36:9

The prophets who spoke about him

DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
No regnal years. Sennacherib's campaign against Judah, when Scripture names him, is fixed at 701 BC by the Assyrian annals.
HORNUNG, KRAUSS AND WARBURTON (2006), FOR TAHARQA
BREASTED (1906), FOR TAHARKA
Chronological table: 688–663 B.C.
T. G. PINCHES, ISBE (1915)
He died "after a reign of at least 26 years, in 667 BC", so came to the throne "about 693 BC".
A commander under Shabaka, called king by a later writer
J. H. Breasted (1906)

Taharqa came north at twenty with Shabaka and became king about thirteen years after 701; Shabaka must have sent him in command, and "the Hebrew writer, reporting the matter at a later date ... supposes him to have been already king". 2 Kings 19:9 [5]
Acting for the reigning Pharaoh before his own reign
W. M. F. Petrie, as reported by T. G. Pinches (1915); Ellicott's commentary; the Pulpit Commentary

Petrie supposed he acted at first for his kinsman Shabataka; Ellicott suggests he commanded in his father's name; the Pulpit Commentary has him ruling from Napata and over Egypt from about 700 with Shabatok as "a sort of puppet-king", succeeding about 693. 2 Kings 19:9 [18][49][50]
Two campaigns of Sennacherib have been run together
A "general opinion" reported by T. G. Pinches (1915)

Pinches reports "a general opinion" that the Assyrian historians, like those of Kings and Isaiah, "have mingled two campaigns made by Sennacherib, one of them being after the accession of Tirhakah". 2 Kings 19:9 [18]

Every passage

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say that Tirhakah's army met the Assyrians, or what became of it.
Scripture does not say that Hezekiah asked Tirhakah for help.
Scripture calls him "king of Ethiopia", never "Pharaoh"; the Pharaoh Rab-shakeh mocked as "this bruised reed" is not named.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
Scholars' viewTirhakah is identified with Taharqa of the 25th (Kushite) dynasty, the "Tarkû, king of Egypt and Ethiopia" of Ashurbanipal's annals. 2 Kings 19:9 [5][18][24]
